title: Construction Site Sign Checklist: Every Safety Sign a Jobsite Needs
body:
Walk your jobsite from the gate in and check off each area below. Most sites need 10 to 20 signs, and the gaps usually show up at the entrance, around overhead work and at fuel and electrical setups.

Plan my site for free

1. Site entrance and fence line

  • ☐ Hard hat area sign
  • ☐ Authorized personnel only sign
  • ☐ All visitors check in sign
  • ☐ PPE required beyond this point sign
  • ☐ No trespassing construction site sign

2. Overhead work, cranes and lifts

  • ☐ Overhead hazard sign
  • ☐ Crane swing radius sign
  • ☐ Stay clear of suspended loads sign
  • ☐ Aerial lift in use sign

3. Excavations, trenches and fall edges

  • ☐ Open excavation sign
  • ☐ Fall hazard keep back sign
  • ☐ Floor opening sign
  • ☐ Guardrail required sign

4. Fuel, power and hot work

  • ☐ No smoking flammable sign
  • ☐ Fuel storage area sign
  • ☐ High voltage keep out sign
  • ☐ Hot work area sign

5. Job trailer and first aid

  • ☐ First aid station sign
  • ☐ Fire extinguisher sign
  • ☐ Emergency contact numbers sign
  • ☐ Eye wash station sign

Rules worth knowing

  • OSHA 1926.200 covers accident prevention signs on construction sites. DANGER signs mark immediate hazards and CAUTION signs mark potential hazards.
  • Signs must be visible when work is going on and removed or covered once the hazard is gone.
  • Use signs alongside barricades and training, not in place of them.

This checklist is a starting point, not legal advice. Check the OSHA standard and your local code for your exact situation.

Common questions

How many signs does a small jobsite need?

Most small residential and light commercial sites need 10 to 20. Start with the entrance, PPE, overhead and fall hazard signs, then add fuel and electrical signs where they apply.

Are aluminum signs better than plastic on a jobsite?

Aluminum holds up to weather, sun and being moved from site to site, and it can be screwed or zip tied to fence and posts.

title: Warehouse Safety Sign Checklist: Signs Every Warehouse and Distribution Center Needs
body:
Warehouses mix people and forklifts in tight space, so most signs go where those two meet. Walk the building in this order and check off what you already have.

Plan my site for free

1. Forklift traffic and aisles

  • ☐ Forklift traffic sign
  • ☐ Pedestrians stay in walkway sign
  • ☐ Stop look both ways sign
  • ☐ Speed limit forklift sign

2. Loading docks

  • ☐ Open dock edge fall hazard sign
  • ☐ Chock wheels sign
  • ☐ Dock plate keep clear sign
  • ☐ Trailer must be secured sign

3. Racking and storage

  • ☐ Do not climb racking sign
  • ☐ Maximum load rack sign
  • ☐ Keep aisles clear sign
  • ☐ Heavy items low sign

4. Battery charging and maintenance

  • ☐ Battery charging area sign
  • ☐ No smoking sign
  • ☐ Eye wash station sign
  • ☐ Lead acid battery sign

5. Exits and fire equipment

  • ☐ Fire extinguisher sign
  • ☐ Do not block exit sign
  • ☐ Keep clear electrical panel sign
  • ☐ Emergency exit sign

Rules worth knowing

  • OSHA 1910.178 covers forklifts, and 1910.176 requires aisles and passageways be kept clear and marked where mechanical handling equipment is used.
  • Exit routes must be marked under 1910.37, and electrical panels need clear working space under 1910.303.
  • Battery charging areas need ventilation, fire protection and eyewash access where battery acid is handled.

This checklist is a starting point, not legal advice. Check the OSHA standard and your local code for your exact situation.

Common questions

Where should forklift signs go?

At every aisle end, pedestrian crossing, blind corner and doorway where forklifts and people share space.

Do loading docks need their own signs?

Yes. Dock edges, dock plates and trailer restraint rules are some of the most common warehouse injury spots.

title: Manufacturing Plant Sign Checklist: Safety Signs for the Production Floor
body:
A production floor needs signs at each machine, each PPE zone change and each place energy is stored. Use this list area by area.

Plan my site for free

1. Machines and moving parts

  • ☐ Moving parts keep hands clear sign
  • ☐ Pinch point sign
  • ☐ Machine guard must be in place sign
  • ☐ Authorized operators only sign

2. Lockout and maintenance

  • ☐ Lockout tagout required sign
  • ☐ Do not operate sign
  • ☐ Energy isolation point sign
  • ☐ Stored energy sign

3. PPE zones

  • ☐ Hearing protection required sign
  • ☐ Safety glasses required sign
  • ☐ Steel toe boots required sign
  • ☐ Respirator required sign

4. Chemicals and compressed gas

  • ☐ Flammable storage sign
  • ☐ Corrosive sign
  • ☐ Compressed gas cylinders sign
  • ☐ Hazardous waste sign

5. Electrical and utility rooms

  • ☐ High voltage sign
  • ☐ Arc flash sign
  • ☐ Authorized personnel only sign
  • ☐ Keep clear electrical panel sign

Rules worth knowing

  • OSHA 1910.145 sets the sign classes: DANGER for immediate hazards, CAUTION for potential hazards, and safety instruction signs for general practices.
  • Lockout tagout under 1910.147 requires energy control procedures. Signs remind workers but do not replace locks and tags.
  • Machine guarding is required under 1910.212. A sign never substitutes for a missing guard.

This checklist is a starting point, not legal advice. Check the OSHA standard and your local code for your exact situation.

Common questions

What color should machine warning signs be?

Use DANGER (red) where contact would cause serious injury right away, and CAUTION (yellow) for potential hazards like pinch points.

Do PPE signs need to be at every entrance?

Post them at each entrance to a zone where the PPE requirement changes, so people see it before they walk in.

title: Restaurant Kitchen Sign Checklist: Safety and Health Signs for Commercial Kitchens
body:
Health inspectors and new hires both look for the same handful of kitchen signs. Go station by station and check off what is already posted.

Plan my site for free

1. Handwashing and food safety

  • ☐ Employees must wash hands sign
  • ☐ Hand sink only sign
  • ☐ Raw meat storage sign
  • ☐ Allergen awareness sign

2. Cooking line

  • ☐ Hot surface sign
  • ☐ Fryer hot oil sign
  • ☐ Hood fire suppression sign
  • ☐ Knife safety sign

3. Walk-in cooler and freezer

  • ☐ Walk in cooler sign
  • ☐ Keep door closed sign
  • ☐ Inside release sign
  • ☐ Slippery floor sign

4. Dish area and chemicals

  • ☐ Chemical storage sign
  • ☐ Do not mix chemicals sign
  • ☐ Eye wash station sign
  • ☐ Wet floor sign

5. Gas, fire and exits

  • ☐ Gas shut off sign
  • ☐ Fire extinguisher sign
  • ☐ Class K extinguisher sign
  • ☐ Do not block exit sign

Rules worth knowing

  • Most state food codes require a handwashing sign at every hand sink used by food employees. Check your local health department code for exact wording.
  • Class K extinguishers are required for cooking with combustible oils and fats under NFPA 10, and a placard near the hood helps staff use it right.
  • Chemical containers need labels under OSHA 1910.1200 (HazCom), and a storage sign keeps chemicals away from food.

This checklist is a starting point, not legal advice. Check the OSHA standard and your local code for your exact situation.

Common questions

Is a handwashing sign required?

In most states, yes, at each hand sink employees use. The exact rule comes from your state food code.

What signs do walk-in coolers need?

A keep door closed sign outside, and an inside release or emergency exit sign inside so nobody gets trapped.

title: Farm Safety Sign Checklist: Signs for Barns, Grain Bins, Livestock and Equipment
body:
Farms have hazards most visitors never think about: grain bins, bulls, chemicals and running equipment. Work through the property in this order.

Plan my site for free

1. Farm entrance and visitors

  • ☐ No trespassing private property sign
  • ☐ Farm equipment crossing sign
  • ☐ Visitors check in sign
  • ☐ Biosecurity no entry sign

2. Grain bins and silos

  • ☐ Grain bin engulfment sign
  • ☐ Confined space sign
  • ☐ Do not enter bin while unloading sign
  • ☐ Lockout auger sign

3. Livestock

  • ☐ Beware of bull sign
  • ☐ Keep gate closed sign
  • ☐ Electric fence sign
  • ☐ Livestock handling area sign

4. Chemicals and fuel

  • ☐ Pesticide storage sign
  • ☐ No smoking fuel sign
  • ☐ Anhydrous ammonia sign
  • ☐ Restricted entry interval sign

5. Shop and equipment

  • ☐ PTO shaft hazard sign
  • ☐ Moving parts sign
  • ☐ Hearing protection sign
  • ☐ Fire extinguisher sign

Rules worth knowing

  • Grain handling rules in OSHA 1910.272 cover bin entry, and engulfment is one of the top causes of farm deaths.
  • The EPA Worker Protection Standard requires posting for certain pesticide applications and restricted entry intervals.
  • Fuel storage areas should be posted no smoking and kept clear of ignition sources.

This checklist is a starting point, not legal advice. Check the OSHA standard and your local code for your exact situation.

Common questions

Do family farms need safety signs?

OSHA rules mostly cover farms with hired workers, but signs at grain bins, bulls and chemicals protect family, visitors and delivery drivers too.

Which farm signs matter most?

Grain bin engulfment, livestock and chemical storage signs prevent the most serious injuries.
